finding: The Spec Requirement selects `specs/request-consistency.md#requirements`, but the Reviewer Request contains no Input snapshot whose filePath is `specs/request-consistency.md`. The selected requirement cannot be compared with its content, so the governing Input set does not support any semantic judgment about that selection.

The selected reference `specs/image-cache.md#preview-cleanup` defines a 24-hour cleanup of documentation-renderer image previews from the preview cache. The What to build section lists the delivered behaviors (Validation Report, Result Summary, invalid-input diagnostic wording, indexed cache lookup, single-scan parser strategy, protected access review, promotion, recovery, runtime migration, and Reader Index Update), and none of them covers preview cache cleanup. The subject states that listing a requirement does not add delivery content, so this selection is unrelated to the delivered work.

Whether the selected `specs/export-retention.md#conditional-export-retention` is delivery content cannot be determined from the request. Its retention requirement applies only when the Reader Index Update target is a generated artifact. No Input states whether `docs/reference/validation-report.md` is generated or manually maintained. ADR 0005 limits its Decision to `本次 promotion artifact retention`, so it is not established that this authority covers a reader-link target. The selection therefore cannot be classified as delivery content.

The two selected requirements give incompatible caller-visible successful results for `promote(inputPath)`. runtime-migration states that the successful result is exactly `{status: "succeeded", artifactId, trackedStateId}`, while result-summary requires the same successful result to include a string `summary` whose value is `${artifactId} promoted to ${trackedStateId}`. Both are selected for this issue, so an implementation cannot satisfy both contracts.

The selected Retention Policy Ownership requirement says a successful tracked artifact is kept for 30 days from the tracked commit and that removal after expiry `不属于本 operation`. ADR 0005 says Readiness only applies the policy and that no other Module creates or changes retention authority. No selected requirement or Input assigns the post-expiry removal to any Module, so the retention obligation has no executor and cannot be implemented or verified as written.

The Promotion Behavior requirement says Readiness must confirm that `artifact.requestId` equals `immutable request.requestId` and that `inputPath` equals the current request's bound artifact path before calling the persistence step, and that Promotion adds no failure branch for this. No outcome is defined for a failed confirmation, so the caller-visible result for a mismatched artifact or path is unspecified in the selected requirements.

The selected Promotion Behavior requirement says expected filesystem failures and rollback failures return `Interfaces 的 structured diagnostic`. The Interfaces are in the Module Design section of the same document, which the selection does not include (it covers only `## Requirements` and its subsections). The selected requirements therefore do not define the failure fields, failure codes, or baselineStatus values that the issue must return.

The Authentication Boundary requirement says Access Review trusts `该 boundary 传入的 verified principal`, and rules/01 says the caller boundary passes the verified principal and the requested operation to the review boundary. The selected requirements never define how Access Review receives the verified principal as an input. The Authorization Behavior requirement also says the decision is the same for every verified principal and depends only on operation. The principal therefore has no defined input channel and no defined effect on any caller-visible result, so the identity requirement cannot be implemented or tested as written.

The Authorization Behavior requirement says that when the operation is allowed, Access Review reads `artifact` and returns `{allowed: true, policyId, bytes}`, but the selected text does not identify which artifact is read or how the request's resourceId maps to the artifact source. That mapping is defined only in the unselected Module Design section, so the read target is not defined by the issue's governing requirements.

The selected Authorization Behavior requirement delegates the result for invalid policy, invalid facts, and Artifact Reader failure to `本文档 Interfaces 的 Other Results 合同`. The Interfaces are in the unselected Module Design section, so the selected requirements alone do not define the failure values, failure codes, or no-read and no-write behavior that the issue must implement.

The selected Complete Operation Contract says invalid `recoverPromotion(input)` input is returned `按 Interfaces 的 Invalid Input Diagnostic 返回`. That diagnostic is defined in the unselected Module Design section of the same document. The selected requirement therefore does not define the failureCode, path, or message of the invalid-input result, so this behavior cannot be implemented from the issue's governing requirements.

The issue delivers Reader Index Update. The selected requirement requires the `docs/readers/index.md` link to change to the new target, the old target to no longer appear, and the new target to appear exactly once with the matching H1 identity. The Acceptance criteria cover only caller-visible behavior verified through public lifecycles and internal algorithm strategies checked by source review, so no acceptance criterion verifies this link change. The delivered change is not gated by the issue's completion conditions.
